brief: An FPV drone pit station for a drone pilot, built in place of the starter base; the viewer is on the side of larger r. Back row at r -1, q 0 to 5, every cell two storeys tall: half-n bases at q 0 and q 5 make two drawer towers, with a drawer on each storey facing the viewer (drawers need half bases on both storeys); full bases at q 1 to 4 carry bins on the top storey, a plain bin at q 1 and divided bins at q 2 to 4, filled with M3 screws, nuts and standoffs. In front, a one-storey deck of covered full bases at q 0, r 1 and at q 1 to 4 on r 0 and r 1 is the work surface. Along the front of the deck, each on its own cover: the radio at q 0, the hex driver set (hexdriver-set) at q 1, the 5-inch quad (quad-5in) at q 2, turned minus 30 degrees (yawDeg -30) so its arms stay on its own cover, the multimeter at q 3 and the goggles at q 4, all on r 1. Cap the open faces and lock the joints.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

result.note: A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base first. Half-n and half-s take any drawer style; half-e and half-w take a slide, swing or long drawer (find_sockets offers those once the half base is on). No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
